claims.text: Hybrid cryogenic rolling followed by warm rolling can simultaneously improve room-temperature strength and tensile ductility in AlCoCrFeNi2.1.
The initial AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a dual-phase lamellar microstructure described as FCC/B2.
Internal boundaries in the initial lamellar colonies are prone to microcrack initiation during tensile loading.
The processing route applies approximately 1.2 strain by cryogenic rolling and another approximately 1.2 strain by warm rolling at 600 °C, for a total strain of approximately 2.4.
Cryogenic rolling is performed at liquid-nitrogen temperature.
Pre- and post-cooling in liquid nitrogen, holding for about 20 minutes between warm-rolling passes, and immediate water quenching are required processing conditions.
Warm rolling at 600 °C promotes localized recrystallization while retaining part of the lamellar morphology.
Hybrid rolling produces a dual heterogeneous microstructure containing nanocrystalline regions and retained lamellar regions.
Cryogenic rolling introduces stored energy that accelerates microstructural transformations during subsequent warm rolling.
Differential strain partitioning between phases with different hardness produces different stored energies and recrystallization driving forces.
The nanocrystalline regions act as barriers to crack propagation.
The nanocrystalline regions enhance strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Retained lamellar regions contribute to load distribution.
The combined heterogeneous structure delays microcrack initiation and propagation and promotes more uniform plastic deformation.
The hybrid-rolled alloy can attain strength approaching 2000 MPa.
The hybrid-rolled alloy can attain approximately 8% tensile ductility together with approximately 2000 MPa strength.
The unmodified lamellar baseline exhibits a strength–ductility trade-off and limited tensile ductility because its internal boundaries facilitate microcrack initiation.
The intervention may apply to other melt-cast eutectic high-entropy alloys having dual-phase lamellar microstructures.
The magnitude of improvement depends on the uniformity of nanocrystalline-region formation and control of processing parameters.
